verdict:
This doesn't reach a fern film yet. The scores average 5.56, and cast is lowest at 4.5. The room still holds together: the door is in the -X wall, the scanner at +X, the duffel at the door end and the case at the scanner end. match (2560) is the best frame here. It is a quiet, lit island with a charcoal case at about 40 and a black duffel at 11, and it would sit in a fern film. wide_pre is still a solid establishing shot, and the clean handbags plate is a clean, well-lit lineup. Four problems hold the stage back, and some out-of-date frames are still in the cut.
1. The question gesture reads as "stop" in two_shot_pre. OfficerA holds his hand out level at Dawn, palm up, with the fingers curled. The camera sees it nearly edge-on, so the curled fingers rise above the knuckles and make the outline of a raised hand. From high behind Dawn in wide_pre, the same hand shows its palm and reads as an offer, so the cut flips its meaning. The escort's open palm in enter is a separate, designed beat: he shows her the bags as the voice says they are already there.
2. Dawn's close-up breaks the luggage match. The case face toward the lens measures a median of 57 graded and 80 raw. In wide_pre, two_shot_pre and match it reads 38-42.
3. The people still look like mannequins. In enter, Dawn's head seen from behind is the largest bright shape in the frame: a smooth dome with the bun bulging out of one side of its outline. In dawn_close her blouse neckline has a jagged pale notch. Her upper arm lies level across the top of the case at shoulder height to grip the strap. The officer's fist in handbags_touch is a smooth mitten with barely separated fingers.
4. The aftermath reads as a neat row of bags on a bench, not a searched room. In empty_ch05 the open duffel turns mid grey (63), so it stops being the black bag from the cold open. The tote is mustard (raw hue about 36 degrees), not cognac.
The folder also still holds the 06:14 renders: wide, two_shot, overhead, empty and tag. Three of them are cut into chapter 04 of the current edit: two_shot (04-09), overhead (04-18) and empty (04-20). All three show the luggage tag outside its insert, and two_shot (like wide) keeps the Ch 00 layout with the tote on the bench. They need re-rendering at this revision, not deleting.
answers:
C35, point by point. I measured graded JPEG medians in boxes I drew myself, so your masks may give different numbers.

1. Does the officer's gesture read as one question across the reverse cut? No. The pose is the same in both frames: one geometry with two meanings. present_to_dawn in apply_pose aims hand_fk.R level at Dawn and then rolls it palm up, and the hand keeps the pose's finger curl of 42. In wide_pre the camera is high behind Dawn and looks down onto the open palm and curled fingers, so the hand reads as an offer. In two_shot_pre the camera sits only a little above the hand, off the end of the bench, and sees it nearly edge-on. The curled fingers rise above the knuckles, the outline becomes a raised hand, and it reads as "stop" or "wait". The cold open does not change who asks. In enter, the open palm belongs to the escort (OfficerB, cheated to (-1.05, -0.82)), turned toward the bags as the voice says they are already there. That is a different, designed beat. OfficerA, who asks in both reverses, keeps his hands behind his back there, and that is right.

2. Do the corrected reverses match? Yes. The case reads 38 in wide_pre and 39 in two_shot_pre, and the duffel reads 20 in both (your figures: 37.2/37.2 and 19.8/19.4). In enter the case and duffel read 31 and 13 (yours: 30.3/10.7); the far case being darker is fine there. In match they read 40 and 11, close to your 42.0/12.0.

3. Does the case in Dawn's answer measure 37.4? Not by my measurement. The case face toward the lens in dawn_close, box (180,520)-(400,680), has a median of 57 graded and 80 raw, and the face runs about 43-70 graded (10th to 90th percentile). In the cold open only the tag insert sits between two_shot_pre and dawn_close, and across that gap the case gets about half again as bright and reads pale grey, not charcoal. In this camera the bench key and the room lights skip the case. Its light comes from the two dawn_close returns linked to the case alone: the lid return at 90 W and the close cloth return at 16 W.

4. Does the tag appear only in its insert? Yes for the frames at this revision: enter, wide_pre, two_shot_pre, dawn_close, match, empty_ch05, handbags and handbags_touch. apply_camera hides the tag and its fittings for every camera except tag. I also checked the floor case in empty_ch05 at 2x. No for the folder as a whole. In the 06:14 frames, empty, overhead and wide show the white tag plainly, and two_shot shows it as a pale sliver on top of the case. wide and two_shot also still carry the tote on the Ch 00 bench. two_shot, overhead and empty are cut into chapter 04 (04-09, 04-18, 04-20), so the problem reaches the film.

5. Does Dawn close her hand around the carry strap in dawn_close? The fingers do wrap the strap between the trolley posts, and it reads as a grip. But the strap sits about 0.56 m above the bench, about 1.42 m from the floor, which is at or just above the shoulder of a 1.68 m woman. hold_carry_strap also solves the elbow with a level pole. Together these lay her upper arm level across the lid, so she reads as hugging the case, not taking hold of it. Her blouse neckline has a jagged pale notch at the collar. Her sculpted hair renders close to the face's value under the key, though its material is already darker (cast.HAIR 0.2 against skin 0.5). With a hard edge at the hairline, it reads as a swim cap.

6. Do the bags stay recognizable? In the 2560 pair, yes. Phase correlation on patches from the tote's lower edge, both handle tabs, the satchel and the shoulder bag gives a best offset of (0,0) every time, so nothing moves by a whole pixel. But the tote is not unchanged in the touch plate. The arm's shadow darkens the top of the front panel by about 31 graded levels just under the rim (native y 560-620), about 23 in the next band, and about 9 by native y 700-800. The handle tabs change by 15-28 levels. Along the sidecar's seam track (within 6 px of it), the two graded frames differ by about 46 on average. The split frame and the red-seam cut must use the clean aec9820 handbags plate, never 03b8bb7. gfx/split.py already reads handbags.png.

7. The split-frame half. I simulated the crop: native (1974, 600) at 0.92 on 958x1080, which covers native x 1453-2494 at the start of the 3% push. The tote's front panel and top seam are plain and continuous. Two things sit on the half's edges:
   - On the left edge, where the halves meet, there is a sliver of the satchel with its strap ring and brass fitting (native x up to about 1555).
   - On the right edge there is the white glove box with its blue nitrile tuft (native x from about 2320). It is a pale neutral block, about 64 graded on its face and 85 on its top, and it competes with the tote.
   The three handbags are placed to register with evidence_table purses for the intercut. The satchel can only leave the half by moving, so it should not move on its own. The glove box is free to move.

8. Do the bags hold their identity across chapters? Not fully. The tote reads mustard or khaki rather than cognac. Its raw front panel has a hue of about 36 degrees, with the blue channel near zero (saturation about 0.99). In empty_ch05 the open duffel reads 63, mid grey, against 11-20 everywhere else, so it no longer reads as the black duffel. The cause is that empty_ch05 has no BAG_RETURNS entry. The bench key lights the open bag fully there, and the matte treatment the reverses get does not apply to it. In wide_pre the duffel is a featureless black block behind the officer's hand, with no straps catching light.

9. Do the handling and the aftermath read as different beats? Only weakly. handbags_touch is a fist with no visible body closing on the handles. The tote's body does not move (below the panel's upper third the two frames differ by 1-3 levels), so it reads as gripping, not handling. The fist is a smooth mitten with barely separated fingers. empty_ch05 differs mainly in that the tote lies on its side, the case stands on the floor and the room is empty. The bags stay in the same tidy row, the duffel's opening is not visible from this camera and the glove box looks neat. At 1280 it reads as another wide of bags on a bench, not as a search. Nothing points toward the linings, though the whole chapter turns on what was in them.

fixes.problem: OfficerA's question hand is held out level at Dawn, palm up, with the fingers curled 42. The camera at the end of the bench sees it nearly edge-on, so the curled fingers rise above the knuckles and make a raised-hand outline that reads as 'stop'. From high behind Dawn in wide_pre the same hand reads as an offer: one pose, two meanings across the cut.
fixes.fix: In POSES['ch00']['OfficerA'], lower 'fingers' from 42 to about 20 and leave the thumb open, so the fingertips stay level with the knuckles when seen side-on. In _reach_point('duffel_hover'), bring the target lower and nearer Dawn (hi.z + 0.05 down to about + 0.02, and a few centimetres further toward -Y) so the hand sits low over the duffel's near edge. present_to_dawn aims hand_fk.R level at Dawn whatever the forearm does. Keep the hand close to the forearm's line so the wrist does not bend back, and keep its palm-up roll. Check both reverses: the palm faces up, the fingertips point toward Dawn, and in two_shot_pre no fingertip rises above the knuckle line.

fixes.problem: The 06:14 renders two_shot, overhead and empty are still cut into chapter 04 (04-09, 04-18, 04-20). All three show the luggage tag outside its insert: plainly on the case in empty and on the floor case in overhead, and as a pale sliver on top of the case in two_shot. two_shot also keeps the Ch 00 layout with the tote on the bench, unlike the two-bag reverses. The 06:14 wide is no longer in the cut.
fixes.fix: Re-render two_shot, overhead and empty at the current revision and republish them. apply_camera already hides the tag and its fittings for every camera except tag, so a plain re-render clears the tag. Do not delete these frames, because the edit uses them. For 04-09, either render two_shot with the two-bag ch11 layout, as two_shot_pre does, or point that cut at two_shot_pre. wide can be re-rendered or dropped from the graded folder.

fixes.problem: The case face toward the lens, box (180,520)-(400,680), reads a median of 57 graded and 80 raw. In wide_pre, two_shot_pre and match it reads 38-42. The case jumps to pale grey on the cut into Dawn's answer.
fixes.fix: In dawn_close the bench key and the room lights skip the case (outside_pair). Its light comes from two returns linked to the case alone: the lid return (first value of BAG_RETURNS['dawn_close'], 90 W) and the close cloth return (fourth value, 16 W, the light at close_return aimed at this face). Lower the close cloth return first, by roughly a factor of three to four, because raw 80 against about 37 is several times the light. Then trim the lid return if the top still stands out. Neither light reaches Dawn, so her face does not change. Re-measure the same box on the graded frame and aim for 38 +/- 2.

fixes.problem: The carry strap sits about 0.56 m above the bench (about 1.42 m from the floor), at or just above her shoulder. Her upper arm lies level across the lid to reach it, so she reads as hugging the case. Her blouse neckline shows a jagged pale notch at the collar.
fixes.fix: hold_carry_strap solves the elbow with a level pole, (0.2, -1.0, 0.0) in case space, which swings the elbow out at shoulder height. Give the pole a strong downward component, for example (0.3, -0.6, -1.0), so the elbow drops below the shoulder and the forearm rises to the strap. If the reach no longer closes with the elbow down, cheat Dawn a few centimetres closer to the case. Check that her upper arm hangs clearly below level and does not lie on the lid. In blouse(), smooth the boundary loop of the cut blouse front, with a relax pass limited to the boundary vertices, so the neckline is a clean curve. Check it at 2x in dawn_close.

fixes.problem: The aftermath reads as another tidy row of bags on a bench, not a searched room. The open duffel's opening cannot be seen from this camera, and the bag reads mid grey (63 graded) instead of black (11-20 elsewhere). The case on the floor sinks to 9.
fixes.fix: The duffel is grey because empty_ch05 has no BAG_RETURNS entry. The bench key lights extra-bag-open fully, and the matte treatment the reverses get (reverse_duffel_inputs) does not apply to it. For this camera, give extra-bag-open the same matte value and zero specular, or exclude it from the bench key and give it a small linked return. Aim for 25 or below graded. Spread the open_zip lips 2-3 cm wider so the opening shows. The tote already lies on its side: turn it so its mouth faces the camera. Pull a dark-brown lining panel (about 0.18 x 0.10 m, 2 mm solidify) out over its lip, with a straight slit along the seam, and give it no accent light, since red belongs to the motion graphics. Add a crumpled pair of blue nitrile gloves beside the tote and tip the satchel onto its back, so the bench looks handled. If wanted, add a small linked return (about 8 W) on the floor case to lift it from 9 toward 18 graded.

fixes.problem: The officer's fist is a smooth stone mitten with barely separated fingers. The tote does not move, so the shot reads as a grip, not as handling the bag (the edit's note for 04-08 says the hand is lifting it).
fixes.fix: index_grip sets only the index finger (knuckle, middle, tip, spread). The close_thumb branch of apply_pose fixes the middle, ring and little fingers at 50-58 degrees with no spread. Stagger the four fingers' curls and give them a slight spread, so that dark gaps and knuckle ridges show at 2560. Wrap the thumb over the handles on the near side. Lift the tote 2-3 cm, with both handles taut, so the shot reads as lifting. handbags stays the clean plate for the split frame and the red-seam cut, because in this plate the arm's shadow changes the tote's top seam.

fixes.problem: The tote reads mustard or khaki (raw hue about 36 degrees, blue channel near zero), not cognac. In the split-frame window, the half also catches the white glove box with its blue tuft on its right edge, a pale neutral block that competes with the tote, and a sliver of the satchel's strap ring and brass fitting on its left edge.
fixes.fix: Bring the tote's grade toward cognac. Its saturation (PROPS['handbag-tote'] sat 1.70) is what drives the blue channel to zero, so lower it, and use less of the +0.025 hue shift. Aim for a raw front-panel hue of about 22-27 degrees, and check that the graded panel does not swing back to the salmon the shift was added to fix. Use the same values as the cognac continuity pass on evidence_table and hotel_room, so the tote is one bag everywhere. For the two handbags cameras, move the bench_gloves dressing out of native x > 2320, or darken it well below the tote. Leave the satchel where it is: the three bags are placed to register with evidence_table purses for the intercut, so it should not move on its own. Re-render handbags and handbags_touch together. split.py refits its tote match on every run.

fixes.problem: Seen from behind in the foreground, Dawn's head is the largest bright shape in the frame: a smooth dome with the bun bulging out of one side of its outline from this three-quarter-back angle. The officers' caps read as pillboxes because their visors catch no light.
fixes.fix: Make the bun smaller and tuck it into the nape, so it stays inside the head's outline from this angle. Her hair material is already darker than the skin (cast.HAIR 0.2 against 0.5); the bench key is what lifts it. Exclude her hair and head from the key in enter through light linking, or pull the camera about 0.3 m back so her head takes less of the frame. Keep the hair a smooth sculpted shell: people._sculpt_hair softened the strand relief because it read as a knit beanie. Give the cap visors an edge that catches a line of light, for example a slightly higher specular on the visor faces or a narrow rim light from the scanner side.

fixes.problem: The duffel reads as a featureless black block behind the officer's hand; its straps and shape are lost.
fixes.fix: Give the duffel a little top light in both reverses, not only in wide_pre. Raise the BAG_RETURNS third value (the duffel return) from 0 to about 15-20 W in wide_pre and two_shot_pre, so its straps and zip line catch light at about 25-30 graded. Re-measure both bodies so they still match each other at about 20.
